correctness.rationale: The exact bivariate factorial generating function exp(lambda z+lambda w+rho zw) yields covariance 4lambda^2 rho+2rho^2. Period-block integrals depend only on adjacent independent Poisson period increments, hence are stationary one-dependent with all moments and satisfy the standard CLT. Period-integrated covariances and Parseval give the stated exact nonnegative Fourier penalty; Fourier uniqueness gives the unique minimizer. Strict positivity of every proper-arc mass gives a strict upper bound, and a smooth positive approximate identity reaches its supremum. A stand-alone verifier passed 64 deterministic Fourier, positivity and quadrature assertions, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source explicitly identifies modulation-dependent asymptotic variance as an open sampler-design question. The result gives a complete and sharp answer for the first nonlinear count observable of the natural Poisson-target subfamily: every seasonality worsens physical-time factorial-pair efficiency by an exact positive H^{-1}-type Fourier penalty, the homogeneous profile uniquely minimizes it, highly concentrated rates approach an explicit upper ceiling, and linear-count averages are completely insensitive. This reveals a genuine observable-dependent limitation of time-change intuition and a quantitative design principle beyond a simple numerical computation.
